missing_information_behavior: Do not recommend electrolyte products by default; assess unusual heat exposure, illness, dietary context and total fluid intake if relevant.
safety_exclusions: Do not imply every workout requires an electrolyte drink.
Do not confuse ordinary hydration needs with a need for supplemental electrolytes.
professional_escalation_conditions: Heat illness symptoms, prolonged exercise despite reported short duration, significant dehydration, kidney/heart disease or prescribed fluid restriction.
population_and_context: People doing short exercise sessions with low-to-moderate sweat loss; routine electrolyte supplements are generally not indicated solely by this activity profile.
dose_constraints: No electrolyte supplement dose from this rule. Encourage ordinary hydration appropriate to thirst and conditions, without a universal volume prescription.
certainty_and_limitations: NIH ODS exercise resources provide context for sports performance products; short low-sweat activity alone is not an indication for supplementation. This justification remains draft pending source passage verification, critical appraisal, certainty assessment and professional review.
